UNVERIFIED. Review state, CI state and merge conflicts of open PRs are not modelled. The promotion model assumes every non-draft open PR is mergeable once the freeze lifts, and the booked merge window of a PR (ISSUE-519) as its ready time.

PROVISIONAL constants: 60-minute promotion lead, 4 market hours between two changes to one container, 0.55 working-day utilization, 6 production changes per day, 8-unit bundle cap, 45-minute proposed window length. None is calibrated; the booked calendar peaks at 5 production changes on one day.
The market-hours function is approximate (Globex open Sunday 22:00Z in CDT and 23:00Z in CST, daily halt 21:00-22:00Z, Friday close 21:00Z).

The item verdict 'ships' comes from a keyword rule on the title and from the targets of the item's open PRs. Step J1 lets the judge correct it from the title and problem text only. A destructive window is also a keyword rule (drop, purge, retire, delete) narrowed to windows that are not deploy-only or verify-only; a new wording can slip through either way.

Candidate bundles are built only from production windows and open PRs. A verify, operator, intake or merge window is never a bundle member. Windows with status Blocked stay in the calendar as live windows.

Slot placement for own-window items is greedy and deterministic, not optimal. It uses the standard start times the board already uses (x:07Z), weekdays only, one production change per start time, and a pseudo-container per item when the item has no PR; collisions between items that touch the same container but have no PR are therefore not detected.

The judge model is opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash. Stability was measured on two pilot rounds and on the judged runs described above; agreement across runs measures the authoring, not the truth. Verdicts for unchanged rows were reused from earlier runs (content-keyed), not rerun.
